summary: Implemented the QA blocker: role-preference points now influence which fully balance-tied candidate teams surface, and preference edits now trigger a full candidate/editor recompute instead of badge-only refresh. Tests and static build pass.
completed_work: Updated `src/lib/optimizer.js` to compute per-candidate preference influence metadata and use it as a soft weighted selector only inside buckets that are already tied on the required balance metrics.
Updated `src/lib/appFlow.js` and `src/main.js` so changing a player's `탱커 / 딜러 / 힐러` points rebuilds the visible 6 candidates and selected editor state immediately.
Refreshed Korean UI copy in `src/constants/copy.js` and `src/lib/render.js` to explain that preference points only affect equally balanced options and do not override tier balance.

Added regression coverage in `test/optimizer.test.js`, `test/appFlow.test.js`, and `test/editor.test.js` proving extreme preference changes can alter surfaced candidates while preserving the mandated ranking precedence.
Updated `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to document the shipped preference-aware tie handling, immediate recalculation behavior, and the non-blocking browser-smoke gap.
Ran the build to regenerate `dist/` from the updated source.
known_gaps: `npm run test:browser` was not run in this environment; the current spec treats that browser/mobile smoke gap as non-blocking.
Preference points intentionally do not become a global ranking key; they only influence candidate surfacing inside already-equal balance buckets.
handoff_notes: Key files for QA review are `src/lib/optimizer.js`, `src/lib/appFlow.js`, `src/main.js`, `test/optimizer.test.js`, `test/appFlow.test.js`, `test/editor.test.js`, `README.md`, and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md`.
The worktree already contained other modified files from earlier round work; I did not revert unrelated changes.
